विप्राज्ञया तथोद्वाहे राज्ञा प्रीत्यार्पितं च यत् ।

content_en:
The wearing of cloth even on a defective day (in certain cases)

That which is [given] at the command of a brāhmaṇa, and at a marriage, and what a king has bestowed out of affection — such cloth, the wise have declared, may be worn even on a censured [day]: on Pitrya (Maghā)[?], on an [inauspicious] vāra (weekday), and so forth. || 12 ||

[ṭīkā] When cloth and the like is given at the command of a brāhmaṇa, at a wedding, or by a king out of pleasure, then it may be put on even without the muhūrta (elected moment) stated above, or even in a censured nakṣatra (lunar mansion), vāra, and so on. || 12 || (Anuṣṭubh)
ocr_review_note: Verse 12 pāda 2: OCR reads 'पिष्ण्ये', resolvable either as पित्र्ये (Maghā, whose presiding deities are the Pitṛs) or as पौष्णे (Revatī); both scan correctly in Anuṣṭubh. पित्र्ये is preferred because verse 10, immediately preceding, lists Revatī among the AUSPICIOUS nakṣatras for donning new cloth, so a 'censured पौष्ण' would contradict it — but the akṣara itself is not legible, and the ṭīkā generalises to 'a censured nakṣatra/vāra' without naming one, so it cannot arbitrate.

तनुगे गुरौ नो मौढ्यादिदुष्टसमयेऽप्यशुभे[?] निमित्ते ॥ ३४ ॥
क्षिप्र, ध्रुव, रेवती, चर, मैत्र, मघा नक्षत्रोंमें तथा लग्नसे दशम सूर्य, चतुर्थ चन्द्र, लग्नके गुरु होनेमें मूल गण्डान्तादि वा केतु-उत्पातदर्शनादि शान्तिक तथा पौष्टिक कर्म करने; नैमित्तिक शान्ति गुर्वस्त, शुक्रास्त, बालवृद्धादि दुष्ट समयमें भी शुभ होती है ॥ ३४ ॥ (व० ति०)
content_en:
[Verse 34, concluding portion; the verse opens in the preceding chunk] …with Jupiter occupying the lagna (ascendant). There is no [bar from] mauḍhya (heliacal combustion) and the other defective times — [the rite holds good] even at an inauspicious[?] juncture, when it is prompted by a nimitta (a specific portent or occasion). || 34 ||

[ṭīkā] In the kṣipra ("swift"), dhruva ("fixed"), Revatī, cara ("movable"), Maitra (Anurādhā) and Maghā nakṣatra (lunar mansion)s, and when the Sun stands in the tenth from the lagna, the Moon in the fourth, and Jupiter in the lagna, one should perform the śāntika (propitiatory) and pauṣṭika (prosperity-giving) rites — for instance on account of birth in Mūla, gaṇḍānta (the junction-point affliction) and the like, or on the sighting of a comet or other portent. Naimittika śānti (propitiation undertaken on the occasion of a portent) is auspicious even at defective times such as the heliacal setting of Jupiter, the heliacal setting of Venus, and the bāla ("infant") and vṛddha ("aged") states [of a planet]. || 34 || (Vasantatilakā)
ocr_review_note: Verse 34 pāda 4: OCR 'शयुमवं' does not resolve to any word. Vasantatilakā requires light–light–heavy in these three positions before 'निमित्ते'; the reading 'ऽप्यशुभे' satisfies both the metre and the ṭīkā's sense ('auspicious even in a defective time'), but it is a reconstruction, not a legible scan. Two further, non-flagged corrections: the chunk opens mid-verse (pādas 1–2 and the first half of pāda 3 are in muhurta_chintamani_pg0047_c01), and the verse number printed by OCR as '॥२७॥' has been corrected to ३४ on the ṭīkā's authority.

content_en:
(36) Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi [Nakṣatra-]

The muhūrta for the oblation of homa
From the Sun's nakṣatra (lunar mansion), counting by threes up to the Moon's nakṣatra: the Sun, Vid (Mercury), Śukra (Venus) and Paṅgu ("the lame one" — Saturn); then the Moon, Āra (Mars), Ijya (Jupiter), Ahi[?] (Rāhu) and Śikhin (Ketu). The homa-oblation is not desirable in [the share of] a malefic. || 35 ||

[ṭīkā] The oblation of homa is stated: perform the homa in the oblation-share of a benefic planet, not in that of a malefic. Counting three by three from the Sun's nakṣatra up to the Moon's nakṣatra, know the oblation to belong, in order, to the Sun in the first three, to Mercury in the next three, and thereafter to Venus, Saturn, the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Rāhu and Ketu. || 35 || (Anuṣṭubh)

The residence of Vahni (fire), and its fruit — agnivāsa
That [current] tithi (lunar day), with one added and joined to the vāra (weekday), is divided by four. When the remainder is guṇa (three) or abhra (zero), the residence of Vahni (fire) is upon the earth: therein a homa makes for happiness. When the remainder is śaśi (one) or yugma (two), [the fire dwells] in the sky and beneath the earth respectively, and there is destruction of the life-breath and of wealth. || 36 ||

[ṭīkā] Add 1 to the current tithi, add the vāra, divide by 4 and keep the remainder. If the remainder is 0 or 3, know the residence of Agni to be in the earth: performing the oblation will bring happiness. If the remainder is 1 or 2, the residence of Vahni is, respectively, in the sky (ākāśa) and in the netherworld (pātāla); performing a homa then destroys the life-breath and wealth. || 36 || (Indravajrā)

The muhūrta for eating the new grain
The new grain is auspicious in a cara ("movable"), kṣipra ("swift") or mṛdu ("soft") nakṣatra and in a good lagna (ascendant) — excluding the nandā tithis, the viṣa-ghaṭī ("poison hour"), the months Madhu (Caitra) and Pauṣa, and the days of Ārki (Saturn) and Bhūmija (Mars). || 37 ||

[ṭīkā] Leaving aside all of these — the months Pauṣa and Caitra, Saturday and Tuesday, the nandā tithis 1, 6 and 11, and the viṣa-ghaṭī (as stated in the marriage chapter) — one should take the first eating of the grain of the new harvest (navānna) in a desired lagna occupied by benefics, and in the cara, kṣipra and mṛdu nakṣatras. || 37 || (Anuṣṭubh)

The muhūrta for building a boat
In the nakṣatras of Yāmya (Bharaṇī), Brāhma[?] (Rohiṇī), Viśākhā, Indra (Jyeṣṭhā), Sārpa (Āśleṣā), Pitrya (Maghā), Īśa (Ārdrā) and Maitra (Anurādhā), on the days of Bhṛgu (Venus), Ijya (Jupiter) and Arka (the Sun), the building of a boat in a good lagna is auspicious. || 38 ||

[ṭīkā] In the nakṣatras Bharaṇī, Rohiṇī, Viśākhā, Jyeṣṭhā, Āśleṣā, Maghā and Ārdrā[?], and on Friday, Thursday and Sunday, one should build a boat (a vessel or dinghy) and the like. || 38 || (Anuṣṭubh)

The muhūrta for vīra-sādhana and the like
In Mūla, Ārdrā, Bharaṇī, Pitrya (Maghā) and Mṛgaśirā, with Saumya (Mercury) [in the lagna] — or Venus in the fourth (sukha) — the lagna being Ghaṭa (Aquarius) and the eighth house unoccupied, there is success in vīra-sādhana (the propitiation of a vīra spirit) and in abhicāra (hostile magical rites). || 39 ||
ocr_review_note: Three flagged loci, none of them in the agnivāsa passage. (1) v.35 pāda 3: OCR 'आगु' for the Rāhu-word — both अहि ('serpent', a standard Rāhu epithet) and अगु scan in Anuṣṭubh, and the ṭīkā fixes the referent as Rāhu, so only the akṣara is at issue. (2) v.38 pāda 1: OCR 'याम्य्यविशाच…' leaves one two-syllable nakṣatra term illegible; Anuṣṭubh requires 16 syllables in the first line, and ब्राह्म (Rohiṇī) both fills the gap and matches the ṭīkā's list, but it is supplied, not read. (3) v.38 ṭīkā: OCR 'आर्द्रारहित' reads either as 'आर्द्रा-रहित' (excluding Ārdrā), which contradicts the mūla's ईश = Ārdrā, or as 'आर्द्रा, राधा' (Ārdrā, Anurādhā), which agrees with it; the two readings invert the sense of the whole rule and the scan cannot arbitrate. NOTE: verse 36, the agnivāsa rule itself, is clean — all four pādas scan exactly as Indravajrā, and the ṭīkā's arithmetic (remainder 0/3 = earth, 1 = sky, 2 = pātāla) independently confirms the emendation शेषे गुणेऽभ्रे (guṇa = 3, abhra = 0) against OCR 'शेषे एणेऽभरे'. Verse numbers ३७ and ३९ were printed by OCR as '२७' and '२९' and are corrected on the ṭīkā's authority.

[This chunk carries only the ṭīkā; the mūla of verse 47, headed "Particular yogas causing the swift death of a sick person", stands at the end of muhurta_chintamani_pg0050_c01.]

[ṭīkā] If a person falls ill in the nakṣatra (lunar mansion)s Ārdrā, Āśleṣā, Jyeṣṭhā, Śatatārā (Śatabhiṣā), Bharaṇī, the three Pūrvās, Viśākhā, Dhaniṣṭhā or Kṛttikā; or on a pāpa-vāra (a malefic weekday); or on a riktā tithi (the lunar days 4, 9 and 14), on the twelfth or on the sixth — then that sick person swiftly meets death. It is especially so when the Moon stands in the 4th, 8th or 12th by transit [from the natal rāśi]. || 47 || (Upajāti)

content_en: On a bhadrā tithi (lunar day — the 2nd, 7th or 12th), on the vāra (weekday) of Ravija (Saturn), Bhūtanaya (Mars) or Arka (the Sun), and in the nakṣatra (lunar mansion) of Rādhā (Viśākhā), Aryaman (Uttaraphālgunī), Ajacaraṇa (Pūrvabhādrapadā), Aditi (Punarvasu), Vahni (Kṛttikā) or Vaiśva (Uttarāṣāḍhā)[?] — there arises the Tripuṣkara yoga, which renders threefold whatever occurs by way of death, of loss, or of increase; and it makes [only] twofold when [the nakṣatra is] Vasu (Dhaniṣṭhā), Tvāṣṭra (Citrā) or Cāndra (Mṛgaśirā). || 50 ||

Pādas 1, 2 and 4 have been recovered and verified syllable by syllable against the Vasantatilakā pattern, and every tithi, vāra and nakṣatra term so recovered is independently confirmed by the ṭīkā. The opening of pāda 3 (OCR 'वेशखेषष्‌ / ष्केरो'), however, yields no metrically admissible reading: a locative such as ऋक्षे or भेषु is required at the junction between वैश्व- and त्रिपुष्करो but cannot be read off the scan, so that junction is flagged.

content_en:
(40) Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi [Nakṣatra-]

[ṭīkā, on verse 50] The bhadrā tithi (lunar day)s 2, 7 and 12; Saturday, Tuesday and Sunday; and the nakṣatra (lunar mansion)s Viśākhā, Uttaraphālgunī, Pūrvabhādrapadā, Punarvasu, Kṛttikā and Uttarāṣāḍhā — when this much of tithi, vāra (weekday) and nakṣatra falls at one and the same time, the Tripuṣkara yoga is formed. If someone dies in it, two more will die in that house; if some article is lost, two more will be lost; if some article is gained or increases, two more will be gained. If, in the place of [those] nakṣatras, Dhaniṣṭhā, Citrā or Mṛgaśirā stands, the said results become twofold — this is the Dvipuṣkara yoga. || 50 || (Vasantatilakā)

Times forbidden for the cremation of a substitute effigy of the corpse
On the days of Śukra (Venus), Āra (Mars) and Ārki (Saturn); on darśa (the new moon), bhūta (the fourteenth) and madana (the thirteenth); on the nandā tithis[?]; in a tīkṣṇa ("sharp") or ugra ("fierce") nakṣatra, in Pauṣṇa (Revatī) or Vāruṇa (Śatabhiṣā); on a Tripuṣkara day; in a deficient (kṣaya) or intercalary (adhika) month; at an ayana (solstitial ingress) — and, if more than a year has passed [since the death], also in the southern (yāmya) course; in the Pāta (Vyatīpāta) and Parigha yogas; when Devejya (Jupiter) or Venus is heliacally set; in Bhadrā and Vaidhṛti; and in the bright fortnight — the cremation of the effigy-image of the corpse is not [to be performed]. || 51 ||

For the performer, the janma and pratyari tārās, and the Moon in the fourth, twelfth or eighth[?] [from his natal rāśi], are not good. In Sanmaitra (Anurādhā), Bhaga (Pūrvaphālgunī), Aditi (Punarvasu), the dhruva ("fixed") nakṣatras, Viśākhā …[?] and Citrā, and on Wednesday, [the act is] admissible as well [though middling]. It is best on the days of Arka (the Sun), Ijya (Jupiter) and Vidhu (the Moon), and in Śruti (Śravaṇa), Kara (Hasta), Svātī, Aśvinī and Puṣya. And all this is to be weighed after the period of impurity has passed; within it, only so far as is possible. || 52 ||

[ṭīkā] When the corpse of one who has died is not recovered, the muhūrta for making the parṇaśara (the leaf-effigy, pratikṛti) is stated: one should not perform the cremation of the parṇaśara on Friday, Tuesday or Saturday; on the fourteenth, the new moon or the thirteenth; on the nandā tithis 1, 6, 11; in tīkṣṇa and ugra nakṣatras, in Revatī or Śatatārā; in the Tripuṣkara yoga; in an intercalary or deficient month; at the Karka and Makara saṅkrāntis; and — if more than a year has passed since the death — also in the dakṣiṇāyana (southern course); likewise in the Vyatīpāta and Parigha yogas, when Venus or Jupiter is heliacally set, in Bhadrā and Vaidhṛti, and in the bright fortnight. || 51 || For the one performing the rite, that day should not be his janma [nakṣatra] or his pratyari tārā, and the Moon should not be in the 4th, 8th or 12th from his natal rāśi. In Anurādhā, Pūrvaphālgunī, Punarvasu, the dhruva nakṣatras, Viśākhā, Mṛgaśirā, Citrā, Dhaniṣṭhā, and on Wednesday, the said act is called middling; while Sunday, Thursday and Monday, and the nakṣatras Śravaṇa, Hasta, Svātī, Puṣya and Aśvinī, are auspicious. All these considerations [apply] after the period of impurity… [the sentence continues in the following chunk]

Chapter 2] With the Hindi ṭīkā (41)

The auspicious and inauspicious fruit of one born in Mūla or Āśleṣā
Others, again, have declared: the first eight ghaṭīs of Mūla and the last five nāḍīs of Śakra (Jyeṣṭhā) [are abhukta-mūla]. One should abandon the child so born; or else the father should not look upon its face for eight years. || 54 ||

[ṭīkā] Other ācāryas say that the 8 ghaṭīs at the beginning of Mūla and the 5 ghaṭīs at the end of Jyeṣṭhā constitute abhukta-mūla. Here, [the other] being the majority opinion, the ācārya has taken Nārada's view alone as authoritative. If a child is born in this abhukta-mūla, it is to be abandoned; or else the father should not look upon that child's face for eight years, and only then, after performing śānti (the propitiatory rite), should he look. By extension, the same consideration applies to the end of Āśleṣā, the beginning of Maghā, and so forth. || 54 || (Upajāti)

In the first pāda (quarter) of Mūla the father meets destruction; in the second, the mother; in the third, wealth. Of the fourth [quarter the fruit] is auspicious; and through śānti it becomes good in every case. In Ahi-bha (Āśleṣā) the order is reversed. || 55 ||

[ṭīkā] If a daughter or a son is born in the first quarter of Mūla, the father perishes; in the second, the mother dies; in the third, there is loss of wealth; if born in the fourth quarter it becomes auspicious once śānti has been performed, and there is doṣa (affliction) to no one. In Āśleṣā this same consideration is inverted — in the fourth quarter the father, in the third the mother, in the second loss of wealth; and the first quarter becomes auspicious after śānti is done. There is a further method: it destroys the father in the 1st year, the mother in the 3rd, wealth in the 2nd, the father-in-law in the 9th, a brother in the 6th, a wife's brother or maternal uncle in the 8th, and other kinsmen not named in the 7th year — therefore it is proper to perform śānti. By yet another method, a special consideration of Mūla and Āśleṣā in the form of a tree or a creeper, by way of laying out a cakra (diagram), is set down in the cakra [tables]. || 55 || (Upajāti)

[Appended cakra tables — the Mūla-puruṣa-cakra, the Mūla-cakra for the birth of a girl, and the Sarpa-vṛkṣa-cakra. Read as: body-part or plant-part — count — result. The scan of these tables is heavily damaged and the three columns are interleaved; only the entries legible in this chunk are given, and their continuation stands in muhurta_chintamani_pg0053_c02.]

Mūla-puruṣa-cakra: at the crown 4 — destruction of cattle; at the mouth 6 — loss of wealth; at the throat 5 — gain of wealth; at the heart 5 — crookedness; at the arm 5 — gain of wealth; at […] 7 — destruction of […][?].
Mūla-cakra for a girl's birth: at the head 5 — […][?]; at the mouth 7 — the father's decease; at the eye 2 — destruction of the mother; at the neck 2 — […][?]; at the shoulder 4 — devoted to elders; at the crown 5 — a king.
Sarpa-vṛkṣa-cakra: at the fruit 10 — wealth; at the flower 9 — wealth; at the leaf 9 — fear from the king[?]; at the branch 7 — loss; at the bark 13 — […][?]; at the nakṣatra 8 — destruction of the lineage.

The other five are all cells of the three appended cakra tables, whose columns are interleaved and partly illegible. The priority passage itself (vv. 54–55: the Mūla/Āśleṣā doṣa and its śānti-parihāra, including the explicit cancellation 'शान्त्या सर्वत्र सत्स्यात्') is otherwise clean — all four pādas of v.55, and pādas 1, 2 and 4 of v.54, verify exactly against the Upajāti pattern.

(42) Muhūrta-cintāmaṇi [Nakṣatra-]

[ṭīkā, on verse 56] In the months Āṣāḍha, Bhādrapada, Āśvina and Māgha, Mūla's residence is in heaven; in Śrāvaṇa, Kārttika, Caitra and Pauṣa, upon the earth; in Phālguna, Mārgaśīrṣa, Vaiśākha and Jyeṣṭha, it dwells in the netherworld. In whichever month it dwells wherever, it produces its inauspicious fruit there alone; elsewhere[?] there is no doṣa (affliction). || 56 || (Indravajrā)

The parihāra (remedy, cancellation) of gaṇḍānta and the other defects
Gaṇḍānta; Indra (Jyeṣṭhā); the yogas Śūla, Pāta, Parigha, Vyāghāta and Atigaṇḍa; the avama (omitted, kṣaya) tithi (lunar day); a saṅkrānti (solar ingress); Vyatīpāta; Vaidhṛti; Sinīvālī, Kuhū and Darśa; Vajra; the fourteenths of the dark fortnight; Yamaghaṇṭa; the Dagdha yoga; the Mṛtyu yoga; Viṣṭi (Bhadrā); the nakṣatra (lunar mansion) of a uterine brother; and the birth[?]-nakṣatra of the parents — [a birth in any of these] is commended as auspicious [only] through śānti (the propitiatory rite). || 57 ||

[ṭīkā] Gaṇḍānta, Jyeṣṭhā, Śūla, Pāta, Parigha, Vyāghāta, Atigaṇḍa, the kṣaya (decayed) tithi, saṅkrānti, Vyatīpāta, Vaidhṛti, Sinīvālī (the earlier half of the bright first tithi), Kuhū (the later half of the dark fourteenth), Darśa (the new moon), the Vajra yoga, the dark-fortnight fourteenth, Yamaghaṇṭa, the Dagdha yoga, the Mṛtyu yoga, Bhadrā, and the birth-nakṣatras of a uterine brother and of the mother and father — the birth of a son or a daughter within this many [conditions] is inauspicious; through the śānti of these it becomes auspicious. By extension, birth during an eclipse, a trika birth (a daughter after three sons, or a son after three daughters), and the like are treated in the same way. || 57 || (Śārdūlavikrīḍita)

Consideration of the number and the form of the stars of Aśvinī and the rest
[The star-counts of the twenty-seven nakṣatras, encoded in bhūta-saṅkhyā:] …[?] …; a hundred; and thirty-two. || 58 ||

[ṭīkā] The tārās (component stars) of the nakṣatras beginning with Aśvinī are stated: Aśvinī 3, Bharaṇī 3, and likewise Kṛttikā 6, Rohiṇī 5, Mṛgaśirā 3, Ārdrā 1, Punarvasu 4, Puṣya 3, Āśleṣā 5, Maghā 5, Pūrvaphālgunī 2, Uttaraphālgunī 2, Hasta 5, Citrā 1, Svātī 1, Viśākhā 4, Anurādhā 4, Jyeṣṭhā 3, Mūla 11, Pūrvāṣāḍhā 2, Uttarāṣāḍhā 2, Abhijit 3, Śravaṇa 3, Dhaniṣṭhā 4, Śatabhiṣā 100, Pūrvabhādrapadā 2, Uttarabhādrapadā 2, Revatī 32. By the counting of these stars, and by the shapes about to be stated, the nakṣatras are recognised. || 58 || (Upajāti)

The forms of Aśvinī and the rest: a horse's face; a yoni; a razor; a cart; a deer's head; a jewel; a house[?]; an arrow; a wheel; a house; a couch; a bed; a hand; a pearl; and coral. || 59 ||

A festal arch; [a heap] resembling a bali-offering; an earring; a lion's tail; an elephant's tusk; and couches… [the verse continues in the following chunk]
